sources.title: National Disaster Risk Management Policy 2024–2033
sources.organization: National Disaster Management Agency, The Gambia
sources.temporal_coverage: Disaster impacts and implementation review through 2022; policy period 2024–2033
sources.methodology: Review of prior implementation, agency interviews and regional consultations.
sources.limitations: No outcome evaluation or household measures.

sources.title: The Gambia National Climate Hazard Assessment: Technical Report
sources.organization: Global Center on Adaptation, with World Bank and Government of The Gambia collaboration
sources.temporal_coverage: Observed reference conditions and modeled climate/flood hazards through 2100, with focus on 2050
sources.methodology: Combines observational data, climate projections and mapped flood scenarios.
sources.limitations: Hazard models do not measure household impacts or conflict outcomes.

sources.title: The Gambia: Climate Policy Diagnostic, High-Level Summary Technical Assistance Report
sources.organization: International Monetary Fund, Fiscal Affairs Department
sources.methodology: High-level summary of IMF technical assistance requested by the Gambian authorities.
sources.limitations: National diagnostic; not a subnational or event-level causal study.

claims.locator: PDF p. 10, disaster and vulnerability context
claims.paraphrase: For the 2022 extreme-rain event, parts of West Coast Region received 276 mm in 20 hours; policy cites a separate World Bank estimate of 80,000 affected in Greater Banjul.
claims.limitations: This remote-assessment estimate is not comparable to OCHA's rapid-needs count.

claims.locator: PDF p. 29, review of the 2008 disaster-risk policy
claims.paraphrase: All eight regions had disaster committees; committees in 56 districts were partly functional, and community committees remained difficult to establish.
claims.limitations: Historical review, not a current functionality audit.

claims.locator: PDF p. 30, institutional performance and implementation challenges
claims.paraphrase: NDMA cites funding, regional logistics/storage, supply pre-positioning, and staffing constraints, often only two decentralized staff.

claims.locator: PDF p. 30, institutional performance and implementation challenges
claims.paraphrase: Unequal agency cash-transfer amounts in one community can create tension and suspicion.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Unequal aid transfers can create community tension (PDF p. 30).

claims.locator: PDF p. 11, impacts of hazards and key challenges
claims.paraphrase: The policy says peripheral drought and desertification drive displacement toward low-lying urban areas.
claims.limitations: No origin or destination counts; not conflict evidence.

claims.paraphrase: By 2050 under moderate emissions, inland historical 25-year extreme-heat events are projected every two years; northeast days above 40°C more than double.
affected_groups: people in inland and northeastern areas

claims.locator: PDF p. 11, executive summary on fluvial flooding
claims.paraphrase: Middle-river floodplains around Mansa Konko, Kuntaur and Janjanbureh have the assessment's highest fluvial hazard.
affected_groups: people and infrastructure in river floodplains
claims.limitations: Mapped hazard, not an affected-resident count.

claims.paraphrase: Current modeled coastal flooding inundates low-lying Tanbi Wetland west of Banjul; the report says its mangroves attenuate flooding inland.
claims.scenario: Modeled baseline coastal flood event with a 10-year return period.
claims.limitations: Ecosystem function, not measured avoided losses.

claims.paraphrase: Under future extreme coastal-flood scenarios, Banjul and Brikama show substantial increases in modeled flood depth compared with current conditions.
claims.limitations: Modeled depths are not observed losses or affected-person counts.

claims.paraphrase: IMF reports that coastal resilience is constrained by an unclear institutional framework, absent land-use policy, and limited technical and institutional capacity.
claims.limitations: This is a high-level national diagnosis without local capacity measures.

claims.paraphrase: IMF states that water insecurity increases pressure for internal migration, which in turn increases deforestation through agricultural expansion and charcoal demand.
claims.limitations: The summary provides no migration totals or violence outcome; this is not a conflict estimate.

access_audit.notes: Opened and read the public 50-page policy, including disaster context and historical implementation review.
Opened the 84-page report and read methods, heat projections and named coastal and river flood passages.
Opened and read the IMF's four-page published high-level summary, including adaptation and water-migration passages.

access_audit.locator: Official IOM DTM report page and linked assessment
access_audit.notes: The official page returned HTTP 403; search-index text and secondary summaries were not used for claims.

access_audit.locator: Full article methods and study-area passages
access_audit.notes: Read the article; its sampled villages and respondents are in Senegal, so it was excluded as The Gambia evidence.

search_audit.query: The Gambia climate vulnerability district community adaptation assessment report local government PDF flood drought
search_audit.outcome: Opened the NDMA policy and 2026 hazard assessment; they name Greater Banjul, West Coast, Tanbi and middle-river localities. The recent IOM local assessment was inaccessible.

search_audit.query: The Gambia climate natural-resource conflict pastoral land water dispute report local communities Gambia climate conflict
search_audit.outcome: The IMF summary links water insecurity with internal-migration pressure; the NDMA review reports community tension from differing aid-transfer values. No opened report established a climate-to-violence link.

search_audit.query: The Gambia political conflict insecurity climate adaptation delivery disaster response access report
search_audit.outcome: NDMA reports funding and decentralized logistics/staffing constraints, but no inspected source connects conflict or insecurity to disrupted climate-service or aid delivery; this is an evidence gap, not evidence of absence.

search_audit.query: The Gambia disaster risk management early warning community preparedness resilience capacity assessment flood report PDF
search_audit.outcome: The NDMA review documents committee functionality and response constraints; the hazard assessment identifies Tanbi mangroves as flood attenuation; IMF describes coastal institutional-capacity gaps.

gaps: The official IOM DTM climate-vulnerability assessment page returned HTTP 403; no claims use search-indexed or secondary text.
The inspected sources report climate exposure, migration pressure and aid-delivery tensions, but do not establish climate-related violence or conflict disrupting adaptation delivery.
The GCA assessment models climate hazards and infrastructure exposure; it does not estimate household vulnerability, conflict outcomes or adaptation delivered.
NDMA's cited 80,000 Greater Banjul estimate comes from a separate 2022 World Bank remote assessment and should not be combined with OCHA rapid-needs totals.
